epitaph

EP-ih-taf · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Epitaph is the words inscribed on a tombstone or monument in memory of the person buried there.

The old headstone's epitaph, worn nearly smooth by two centuries of rain, simply read, "Beloved by all who knew her."

Worked Example

For his epitaph, the retired sea captain had chosen a single line from his favorite sailing poem, carved beneath his name and the years of his life.

An epitaph is the short written inscription itself -- the words carved in stone -- rather than the ceremony or a poem read aloud at a funeral.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

inscription: An inscription is any words carved, engraved, or written onto a surface -- a ring, a trophy, a book's flyleaf, a cornerstone. An epitaph is one special kind of inscription: the words on a tombstone remembering the person buried beneath it. Every epitaph is an inscription; few inscriptions are epitaphs.

memorial: A memorial is anything made or done to keep a memory alive -- a statue, a scholarship, a moment of silence. An epitaph is narrower and always written: the brief line carved on a grave marker. A memorial can fill a park; an epitaph fits on a stone.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

birth announcement: a notice celebrating the arrival of a new baby

christening: a ceremony marking a baby's naming and welcome

Where it sits · how grand the tribute is — label → epitaph → monument

label vs. epitaph: A label is the humblest text of all -- a name on a folder, a price on a jar -- identifying without honoring, far below the weight of memory an epitaph carries.

monument vs. epitaph: A whole monument is built and dedicated to a memory, far more elaborate than a single carved epitaph.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — epi-

Prefix — epi-: upon, above (Greek)

Root — taph

Root — taph: tomb (from Greek taphos, 'tomb')

Put it together

Put it together: Epitaph comes from Greek epi- ("upon") + taph ("tomb," from Greek taphos) -- literally "upon the tomb," the words placed on a grave marker.

Use the root in a new word: cenotaph

Use the root in a new word: cenotaph: A cenotaph is literally an 'empty tomb' -- a monument raised for someone whose remains rest elsewhere, built on the same Greek taphos ('tomb') that ends epitaph.

Word Choice

An epitaph is short, carved in stone, and permanent -- often the very last words associated with someone, sometimes chosen to be humorous, humble, or deeply personal.
